Sol.scope: Retrospective evaluation of the existing single Sol delivery only. No new generation or manual audio edits.
Sol.aggregation: Equal anchor weights within each item; retain partial credit. Sum items; engineering cap unchanged.
Sol.strict_auxiliary: All four reliable anchors within +/-2 frames, independently of graded score.
Sol.source_mapping_maximum: Diagnostic only; does not zero a correctly timed utterance because another contextual candidate contains a short duplicate source interval.
Sol.content_gate: No whole-utterance completeness gate. Actual absent target audio at an anchor receives zero. Inconclusive matching is pending with score bounds, not assumed failure.
Sol.timing_evidence: Stable normalized acoustic matching on actual exported MP4 against original authorized dialogue reference; not a certified phoneme/viseme metric.
Sol.visual_applicability: Assistant inspection of contextual source frames and exact anchor frames; not human-certified labels or measured lip motion.
Sol.threshold_status: Prospective human calibration pending. These are explicit pilot thresholds, not thresholds claimed by a paper or universal production standards.
Sol.development_set_notice: The previous Sol result was reviewed before this protocol was designed. This is a development-set retrospective sensitivity test.

T01.reason: Robot/character shot; no reliably readable human lip articulation.

T03.reason: Male speaker remains visible at all four selected anchors; later reaction cut not treated as speaking mouth.

T04.reason: Female reaction/over-shoulder projection while male line continues; no speaker lip anchors.

T06.reason: Female close-up switches to a distant two-shot; later lip detail insufficient at review resolution.

T07.reason: Begins over shoulder; changes to male face for the remaining anchors.

T08.reason: Male line continues across a female reaction shot.

T09.reason: Female face is visible at the selected anchors after the brief prior shot.

T10.reason: Female close-up at selected anchors; later cuts to male reaction.

T11.reason: Exact-anchor frames retain the female speaker/holographic face at all four anchors; the male reaction occurs after the last anchor.

T12.reason: Male mouth obstructed by robot hand; assess phrase location, not visible lip motion.

historical_other_models: Two-frame whole-item binary rule retained; not rescored in this update.
